summary: Code-quality review of the server-side paid-duel region eligibility change. Read the full working-tree diff against HEAD (d5bb5e3) myself rather than trusting the upstream file lists, read every changed file in full, and independently re-ran app lint (clean), app typecheck (clean), app tests (80 files / 745 tests green) and a full `next build` whose route table shows both /duel and /duel/chips as dynamic. No critical findings. The refactor is well factored: assertPaidDuelAllowed is a genuine one-line delegate with zero logic change, the allow-list and fail-closed ordering are byte-identical, the kill-switch + geo composition now lives in exactly one place (the old duplicate kill-switch check in the edge route is gone), and rankedEligibility.ts stays import-clean for the edge runtime. Every changed control has a non-test caller (rankedEligibility.ts: 3, DuelHome/ChipDuelLobby: 1 each). All five open items handed to me were checked and resolved: (1) the GeoHeaderSource case-insensitivity reliance is safe — both real call sites are Headers/ReadonlyHeaders AND the literals are already lowercase, so even a case-sensitive source would work; (2) the missing component render test is a genuine pre-existing gap but non-blocking; (3) `!geoAllowed` is provably equivalent to `geoAllowed === false` because setAllowed is only ever called with a boolean; (4) force-dynamic has no effect on buildMetadata (pure) and does not break the Suspense/useSearchParams boundary — it makes it a no-op during SSR; (5) metadata exports and Suspense boundaries are otherwise untouched. I also confirmed no next.config/middleware Cache-Control override could defeat force-dynamic. Two warnings and seven info findings recorded, none blocking. Read-only: no files changed except reverting the app/next-env.d.ts churn my own build produced.
goal: Code-quality review (correctness, design, maintainability, conventions, regression surface) of moving paid-duel region eligibility to server-side determination at request time on /duel and /duel/chips.

verifiedIndependently.claim: assertPaidDuelAllowed is a one-line delegate with unchanged allow-list contents and fail-closed ordering
verifiedIndependently.method: Read app/src/lib/paidDuelGeo.ts in full and diffed against HEAD. The entire body of the old function moved verbatim into decidePaidDuelGeo; enforcementOn() -> !country (missing_geo) -> US region allow-list -> ALLOWED_COUNTRIES ordering is byte-identical, ALLOWED_US_REGIONS (26 entries) and ALLOWED_COUNTRIES (empty) are untouched.

Traced both branches. Old: { allowed:false, reason:'disabled' } | { allowed: geo.allowed, reason: geo.reason ?? null }. New: resolveRankedEligibility returns exactly those two shapes. decidePaidDuelGeo's country/region are re-mapped away, so they still do not leak to the client.
Ran `pnpm build` in app/ myself; route table shows `ƒ /duel` and `ƒ /duel/chips`. Then reverted the app/next-env.d.ts churn per the software-engineer's flagged pitfall.
pnpm lint (clean), pnpm typecheck (clean), pnpm test (80 files / 745 tests passed, 8.38s — no suite-runtime regression).

Repo-wide grep for useRankedEligibility / geo/ranked / geoAllowed / assertPaidDuelAllowed / decidePaidDuelGeo / resolveRankedEligibility / DuelHome / ChipDuelLobby. DuelHome and ChipDuelLobby each have exactly one caller (their page.tsx). assertPaidDuelAllowed's four money-moving callers (paidDuelGuards.ts, tournaments checkout, tournaments register, duel/chips/match) are untouched. No other surface consumes the geo decision.

Checked app/next.config.js headers()/rewrites()/redirects() and confirmed no middleware.ts exists. The only global header rule is securityHeaders on /(.*) — no Cache-Control / s-maxage override, so Next's dynamic-route `private, no-cache, no-store` stands.

findings.issue: Two effects write the same `allowed` state with no ordering discipline. The revalidation effect is keyed on [enabled] only, so when `serverAllowed` changes in place (an RSC re-render / router.refresh() that updates the prop without unmounting), the re-seed effect at :35 fires but the in-flight fetch from mount is neither cancelled nor restarted. A stale response can then land after the re-seed and overwrite a newer, MORE RESTRICTIVE server answer with the older permissive one. I could not construct a concrete real-world trigger (it needs the geo answer to actually change while the component stays mounted, and nothing in DuelHome/ChipDuelLobby calls router.refresh()), which is why this is a warning and not critical — but it is a latent allow-after-deny ordering hazard in the one hook that gates a compliance decision.
findings.fix: Add `serverAllowed` to the revalidation effect's dependency array. That makes the cleanup set `cancelled = true` on the stale request and restarts the probe against the fresh server answer, and it lets you delete the separate re-seed effect at :35-37 (the state can then be keyed off serverAllowed in one place instead of two).

findings.issue: `resolveRankedEligibility` returns a three-way `reason` ('disabled' | 'not_allowlisted' | 'missing_geo') and both pages destructure only `{ allowed }`, throwing it away. Both components then render region-specific copy — 'Not available in your region.' / 'Region restricted … restricted to approved markets only' — for ALL of them, including `reason === 'disabled'`. With the PAID_DUELS_ENABLED kill switch off but NEXT_PUBLIC_PAID_DUELS_ENABLED on, a player in an explicitly allow-listed state (e.g. CA) is told their region is blocked. The behaviour is pre-existing (the old client probe also read only `allowed`), but this change is exactly where the true reason first became available server-side at zero cost, and this is the one release where fixing it costs one extra destructured field.
findings.fix: Pass `reason` down alongside `allowed` and branch the copy: 'disabled' -> a neutral 'Chip duels are temporarily unavailable.' ; 'not_allowlisted' | 'missing_geo' -> the existing region copy. If you deliberately want to keep the kill switch indistinguishable from a region block, say so in a comment at the destructuring site so the next reader does not treat it as an oversight.

findings.issue: Two different types named `RankedEligibility` now exist: the hook's local `{ allowed: boolean }` and the lib's exported `{ allowed: boolean; reason: RankedIneligibleReason | null }`. No conflict today (the hook's is module-private), but if the reason-threading fix above is done, importing the exported one into the hook file collides with the local declaration.
findings.fix: Rename the hook-local interface to something like `RankedEligibilityState`, or drop it and inline the return type.

findings.issue: `NextResponse.json(resolveRankedEligibility(request.headers))` serialises the internal `RankedEligibility` type directly, so that interface is now the public JSON contract. Adding a field to it for internal reasons silently changes the API response. The old code enumerated the fields explicitly, which made that impossible by accident.
findings.fix: The comment in rankedEligibility.ts already documents the coupling, which is why this is info and not a warning. If the type grows internal-only fields later, re-introduce an explicit projection in the route.

findings.issue: Verifier open item 1, resolved. The `GeoHeaderSource` doc says 'case-insensitive header lookup', but decidePaidDuelGeo never relies on that: it passes the already-lowercase literals 'x-vercel-ip-country' and 'x-vercel-ip-country-region'. Both production call sites do provide case-insensitivity anyway (NextRequest.headers is a Fetch API Headers; next/headers' headers() returns ReadonlyHeaders, which is Headers-backed), and HTTP/2 lowercases header names on the wire. So the reliance is not fragile — it is not even load-bearing.
findings.fix: Optional: soften the interface doc to 'header lookup by lowercase name' so a future reader does not think decidePaidDuelGeo requires a guarantee it never exercises. The test double in rankedEligibility.test.ts:19-26 is strictly more capable than the contract needs, which is fine but means its case-folding branch is never distinguishing.

findings.issue: For qa-acceptance: the software-engineer's suggested acceptance check ('curl the page and assert the FIRST HTML contains the region copy') works for /duel but will FALSE-ALARM on /duel/chips. ChipDuelLobby gates on `!user` BEFORE `!geoAllowed`, and useAuth() resolves client-side only, so the server-rendered HTML for an unauthenticated request is always the SignInGate, never 'Region restricted'. The load-bearing property still holds — the stake picker and 'Find match' require `user && geoAllowed`, and geoAllowed is server-truth from render 0 — it is just not observable by curl on that route.
findings.fix: Assert the /duel first-HTML case by curl (DuelHome's mode cards render outside the auth gate, so 'Not available in your region.' is genuinely in the initial bytes when NEXT_PUBLIC_PAID_DUELS_ENABLED=true). For /duel/chips, verify with an authenticated browser session and assert the stake picker never appears at any point, including the first frame.

findings.issue: Narrative accuracy, not a code defect. Both upstream handoffs describe the pre-change static HTML for /duel as 'a build-time shell with the paid mode cards in their optimistic available state'. That is very likely overstated: DuelHome calls useSearchParams(), which de-opts the enclosing Suspense boundary during a static prerender, so the prerendered HTML for /duel almost certainly contained the (empty) Suspense fallback rather than 'available' mode cards. Similarly /duel/chips would have prerendered the SignInGate, since useAuth() has no user at build time. The real defect the change fixes is still entirely real and still exactly as described in the learnings — the CLIENT state defaulted to null and `geoAllowed === false` rendered that as allow — but the 'shipped HTML showed it as available' framing should not be promoted to the ledger as established fact without an empirical check of the HEAD build output.
findings.fix: No code change. If the orchestrator promotes the software-engineer's first learning to a permanent file, trim the HTML claim to what was actually measured (both routes were `o`/static) and keep the accurate part: a tri-state compliance gate rendered as `x === false` is an allow-by-default.

findings.issue: Both routes moved from static (served from the full route cache) to per-request SSR. /duel is a primary hub. This is unavoidable and correct for a per-request compliance decision, not a regression to fix — recording it so a future 'why did /duel TTFB change' investigation finds the cause immediately. Note force-dynamic also makes the Suspense boundary in page.tsx a no-op during SSR, which is a small improvement: `?mode=chips` is now honoured in the server-rendered HTML instead of defaulting to 'quick' and being corrected on hydration.
findings.fix: None. Keep the Suspense wrapper — useSearchParams still needs it if the route ever loses force-dynamic.

findings.issue: Readability nit: the delegate `assertPaidDuelAllowed` is declared above the `decidePaidDuelGeo` it calls. Correct (function declarations hoist) but reads backwards — the one-liner appears before the thing it explains.
findings.fix: Move decidePaidDuelGeo above assertPaidDuelAllowed so the file reads core-then-adapter.

findings.issue: `useRankedEligibility`'s first parameter is now semantically 'should we revalidate', not 'is this feature enabled', and the two call sites disagree: DuelHome passes PAID_DUELS_ENABLED_PUBLIC, ChipDuelLobby hardcodes `true`. Pre-existing inconsistency, harmless (a revalidation fetch on a page where paid UI is hidden costs one edge request), but the hook's otherwise-thorough JSDoc documents `serverAllowed` and never mentions `enabled`.
findings.fix: Add one JSDoc line for `enabled` ('gates the revalidation probe only — it can never make the gate more permissive'), and consider making ChipDuelLobby pass PAID_DUELS_ENABLED_PUBLIC for symmetry.

resolvedOpenItems.resolution: Safe. Both call sites are Headers-backed AND the lookup literals are already lowercase, so the guarantee is not even load-bearing. Documented as info finding, not blocking.

resolvedOpenItems.item: No component render tests for DuelHome/ChipDuelLobby with initialGeoAllowed
resolvedOpenItems.resolution: Agreed non-blocking. Pre-existing gap, not a regression, and the prop threading is enforced by a REQUIRED prop plus a clean typecheck. Routed to qa-acceptance as a manual acceptance check instead (see the /duel/chips SignInGate caveat above).

resolvedOpenItems.item: Is `geoBlocked = paidEnabled && !geoAllowed` equivalent to the old `geoAllowed === false`?
resolvedOpenItems.resolution: Yes, provably. `allowed` is `useState<boolean>(serverAllowed)` and setAllowed is only ever called with `serverAllowed` (boolean) or with `data.allowed` behind a `typeof data?.allowed === 'boolean'` guard, so it can never be null/undefined and `!geoAllowed` is exactly `geoAllowed === false`. I also walked the paidEnabled interplay in all four kill-switch combinations (server on/off x public on/off) and every one produces the same rendered outcome as before the change.

resolvedOpenItems.item: force-dynamic side effects on buildMetadata / Suspense
resolvedOpenItems.resolution: None. buildMetadata is a pure synchronous object builder with no request or build-time dependency, and the static `metadata` export is unaffected by rendering mode. The Suspense boundary is retained and becomes a no-op during SSR (a small improvement for ?mode=). Also checked that nothing downstream can re-cache the response: no middleware.ts, and next.config.js sets no Cache-Control.

resolvedOpenItems.item: Any other regression in the two page.tsx files
resolvedOpenItems.resolution: None. Diff confirms the metadata exports, buildMetadata calls, paths, and the Suspense boundary are byte-identical; the only additions are the headers() import, the resolveRankedEligibility import, the dynamic export, async-ing the component, and the prop.

learnings.insight: Seeding client state from a server prop with `useState(prop)` plus a separate `useEffect(() => setState(prop), [prop])` re-seeder creates two independent writers to one piece of state. If a second effect (here a revalidation fetch) writes the same state but is keyed on different deps, the re-seed and the in-flight response race, and the stale one can win. The hazard is invisible in tests because it needs a prop change while the component stays mounted.
learnings.action: When a value is both server-seeded and client-revalidated, put the server value in the revalidation effect's dependency array too, so its cleanup cancels the stale request and the probe restarts against the fresh seed. One effect keyed on the seed beats two effects racing on the same setState.

learnings.insight: Moving a decision to the server does not make it observable in the first HTML if an earlier conditional in the same component depends on client-only state. ChipDuelLobby gates `!user` (client-only Firebase auth) before `!geoAllowed`, so /duel/chips server-renders the SignInGate for every anonymous request no matter what the geo decision is. The security property still holds — the gated UI needs `user && geoAllowed` — but a curl-based acceptance assertion on that route would report a false failure.
learnings.action: Before writing a 'assert X appears in the first HTML response' acceptance criterion, trace every conditional ABOVE X in the render tree and confirm none of them depends on client-only state (auth, localStorage, window). If one does, assert the negative instead: that the gated element never appears in any frame.

learnings.insight: A Next.js static prerender does not render a client component that calls useSearchParams() — it emits the enclosing Suspense fallback instead. So `o` in the build route table does not by itself prove what the shipped HTML contained; it only proves the route was cached. Both upstream handoffs inferred 'the HTML showed the feature as available' from the `o` marker alone, which is a reasoning step the route table does not actually support.
learnings.action: When the claim is about what bytes users received, read the prerendered artifact (.next/server/app/<route>.html) rather than inferring it from the route-table marker. Reserve the route table for the question it actually answers: static vs dynamic.

learnings.insight: This branch has diverged far enough from main that `git diff main...HEAD` returns ~1.7MB of unrelated pack/skill churn and is useless for review. The change under review was entirely uncommitted, so `git diff HEAD -- app/` plus reading the untracked files was the correct scope.
learnings.action: On a long-lived feature branch, establish the review scope from `git status` first. If the work is uncommitted, diff against HEAD and read untracked files explicitly — diffing against the default branch will bury the change.

learnings.insight: Confirmed the software-engineer's next-env.d.ts pitfall a third time: my own `pnpm build` in app/ re-modified app/next-env.d.ts. Also confirmed DATABASE_URL and DIRECT_URL are already present in this environment's shell profile, so no build-time env setup is needed. App suite: 80 files / 745 tests in 8.38s — no runtime regression versus the pre-change 79/738.
learnings.action: Anyone running `pnpm build` in app/ must follow it with `git checkout -- app/next-env.d.ts` before handing off.
